_method: Hand key for corpus_precision_sample_after.json -- a second uniform random sample (seed 20260726, n=40, distinct from the frozen before-sample's seed 20260725/n=60) drawn from the corpus AFTER data/pipeline/glosses.py's redirect fix and a full excerpts.py regeneration (--per-book-cap 20, matching the original build). Judged by hand, reading only word+text, against PRECISION-STANDARD.md's standard: does the passage supply an explicit or strongly implicit cue (synonym, restatement, apposition, stated contrast, categorical list, functional definition) for the word's meaning-as-used-here, or does it merely fail to contradict a meaning the reader already carries in.
_calibration_note: 18/40 = 45.0% informative. The before-fix frozen key measured 30/60 = 50.0% (95% CI 37.3%-62.7%); this after-fix sample's own 95% CI is roughly 29.6%-60.4% (n=40, p=0.45). The two intervals overlap almost entirely -- this sample gives no statistical evidence that headline precision moved, in either direction. That is consistent with, not a refutation of, the fix: the sense-redirect in glosses.py measurably removed specific wrong-sense claims (confirmed directly -- 'dashed', the PRECISION-STANDARD.md worked example of a wrong-sense claim competing with a more available sense, no longer even registers as a gloss-overlap candidate under the fixed code) and modestly raised band coverage (2+ excerpts: 4.8% -> 5.5%, driven by 22,650 of 30,000 target words now getting *some* correct gloss versus 18,452 before -- more words resolved, not just fewer resolved wrong). But the fix targets word-sense selection, and PRECISION-STANDARD.md's own provisional breakdown on the before-sample found that failure mode was only ~7% of false claims (2/30); the dominant one (~93%, 28/30) was 'right sense, no real cue' -- gloss-overlap treating topical/lexical proximity as if it were explanation. This sample confirms that finding rather than overturning it: of the 22 claims judged not-informative here, essentially all are coherent, correctly-sensed uses with no actual teaching cue (a4 'nearest', a26 'ceiling', a28 'growl', a30 'lamp' -- ordinary words used plainly, nothing wrong with the sense, nothing explaining it either), not wrong senses or non-words. Two considered-and-rejected further levers, recorded so they are not re-proposed at full price: (1) restricting gloss-overlap to a local window near the candidate word, mirroring how apposition/definition-marker are already forward-window-restricted -- measured directly against this same before-sample's 28 rejected gloss-overlap claims and their true-positive counterparts: 13/28 (46%) of false claims have their overlapping word within 100 characters, but so do 13/28 (46%) of *true* positives (several worked examples in PRECISION-STANDARD.md, e.g. 'compliment' at 450 characters, are real teaching cues that span most of an 80-200 word window) -- a locality cutoff removes true and false claims at a statistically indistinguishable rate in this sample, which is the same cliff-not-dial shape as the two already-refuted plans, measured before building anything. (2) A structural rewrite of gloss-overlap into a stronger cue detector (e.g. requiring the overlap word to sit inside an explanatory clause, not just anywhere in the window) is plausible but is a signal redesign, not a pipeline bug fix, and is out of this track's scope -- named as the honest next lever rather than attempted here.
